source_row.stem: A client's vitamin B12 level is significantly below normal, and a family member assumes this deficiency would mainly cause bone-related problems rather than affecting the blood or nervous system. The nurse should recognize this as a possible cause of:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Larger-than-normal red cells and possible nerve-related symptoms tied to how this vitamin supports red cell formation","B":"Hypercalcemia, an electrolyte disturbance not typically caused by a deficiency of this particular vitamin","C":"Microcytic anemia, a pattern more typically associated with iron deficiency than with this particular vitamin's deficiency","D":"A finding generally considered to carry no clinical significance despite the vitamin's role in red cell production and this level being significantly low"}}
source_row.rationale: Vitamin B12 deficiency can cause macrocytic (megaloblastic) anemia and, if prolonged, neurological symptoms such as peripheral neuropathy, distinguishing it from the microcytic pattern of iron deficiency.
